title: Choreography runtime guardrails for composed tool invocations and streaming outputs
creator: Marco Lee
description:
Summary:
This ticket scopes and implements runtime-level guardrails for composed tool invocations where multiple tools (functions/plugins) are chained, their results injected back into the LLM context, and outputs are streamed to callers. Goals are to: (1) prevent runaway recursion/loops when tools call back into the model or other tools, (2) ensure deterministic result injection semantics for structured outputs (function calls) during streaming, and (3) provide a backward-compatible compatibility layer for older tool contracts used by legacy integrations.

Motivation & background:
- We increasingly support multi-tool choreography patterns: model prompts instruct the runtime to call one tool (e.g., a DB fetch), then based on results call another (e.g., a computation or external API). Tools may return structured payloads or partial streaming fragments.
- Without runtime constraints, simple cycles (tool->model->tool) can create infinite loops, amplified costs, and unclear provenance.
- Existing tickets addressed parts of this domain (chaining semantics, result provenance, tool loop quarantine) but we need a cohesive runtime component that unifies streaming contracts and compatibility with older tool APIs.

Requirements (non-exhaustive):
1) Loop detection & mitigation
   - Track an invocation graph per top-level request: nodes=tools/models, edges=invocations. Persist minimal provenance metadata in the request context (tool-key, short call hash, depth).
   - Enforce configurable depth and revisit thresholds: default max depth=6, revisit limit=1 for the same tool-call fingerprint.
   - Provide graceful degradation when hitting limits: return a structured sentinel in streaming output ("tool_quarantine_exceeded") and trigger automatic fallback policy (use local cache or alternative model).

2) Streaming + structured output consistency
   - When a tool supports streaming responses, the runtime must interleave tool-stream chunks into the model stream while preserving structured-function-call boundaries.
   - Define a minimal framing layer for stream events: [meta:start_call], [meta:chunk], [meta:end_call], [meta:inject_result]. This must be expressible in existing SDKs without breaking current parsers.
   - Injection semantics: for function-call based tools, the final structured payload is only injected into the model's KV/prefix once the tool returns its final [meta:end_call] unless the tool is annotated as "partial-inject-allowed". In the latter case, partial JSON fragments are injected into a temporary buffer with strong versioning to avoid double-application.

3) Compatibility layer for legacy tool contracts
   - Some integrations expect synchronous tool calls with inline string blobs. Provide a compatibility adapter that: (a) exposes the old sync endpoint, (b) translates streaming fragments to a buffered sync response within a latency-budget, (c) emits deprecation warnings in logs and the Console.
   - Allow customers to opt into strict-mode (fail on deprecated contract use) via route config.

4) Observability & debugging
   - Add per-request breadcrumbs with redaction-safe traces for each tool invocation, its call-hash, start/end timestamps, and whether a loop quota was applied.
   - Surface loop-guard triggers in Console traces and a limited retention investigation view for incidents.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- We store only compact provenance (call-hash + depth) to avoid heavy memory use in long-lived streams. This avoids full trace embedding but still allows robust loop detection.
- Default depth=6 chosen from benchmarks on typical multi-tool flows; we will expose this as a policy knob for dedicated/private customers.
- Partial injection complexity: supporting partial-inject-allowed introduces non-determinism for downstream evals. To mitigate, partial injections are versioned and the Console will flag prompts that used partial injection for evals and regression alerts.
- Compatibility adapter increases runtime code surface and latency for legacy clients but is critical to avoid breaking large customers during rollout. We'll gate the adapter behind a per-customer feature flag.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit+integration tests that simulate: linear tool chains, cyclic tool chains, tool->model->tool recursion, and many concurrent streaming tool calls.
- E2E regression test against legacy sync-tool contract using the compatibility adapter.
- Console tracing shows breadcrumbs for tool invocations and highlights when loop-guards fired.
- Performance: median latency increase for non-tool requests < 1ms; tail impact measured and documented.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Spec: finalize streaming framing events and injection semantics. (Docs: Confluence doc link below).
2) Runtime: implement provenance layer (compact graph), depth/revisit checks, and stream framing handling.
3) Adapter: implement compatibility shim for legacy sync contracts.
4) SDKs: add framing helpers for JavaScript/Python to emit/parse framing events.
5) Console: surface loop-guard triggers and deprecation notices.
6) Tests & rollout: staged rollout with feature flagging, canary on internal orgs, monitor cost/latency.

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/RUNTIME/Streaming+Tool+Choreography+Guardrails (draft)
- Spike notes + microbenchmarks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A_example_spike_notes
- Prototype PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4231
- SDK helpers draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/118

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: False positives in loop detection might break legitimate deep workflows. Mitigation: conservatively low default thresholds, per-org override, and transparent console UI to apply temporary increases.
- Risk: Partial injection creates divergent model state across retries. Mitigation: idempotency tokens and injection versioning; prefer final-inject default.
- Risk: Compatibility adapter resource cost. Mitigation: enable adapter only for customers with legacy flag and track its usage via metrics.

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- [Owner: Aisha] Draft streaming framing RFC and post to /dev-meta by 2025-11-15.
- [Owner: Marco] Add compact provenance header to request context in runtime prototype (PR link above).
- [Owner: Platform SRE] Add metric hooks for loop-guard triggers and per-route invocation depth histogram.
comments: 2025-11-13 Aisha Kumar: Initial implementation spike attached to PR #4231. Prototype demonstrates framing events merging tool streams into model stream. Observed 0.8ms median overhead on a simple echo workload.

2025-11-14 Marco Lee: Reviewed prototype. Need to change call-hash to be deterministic across language SDKs (use sha1 of tool-key + normalized args). Also add a TTL to provenance entries to prevent unbounded growth in very long streams.

2025-11-16 Product review (Nina Patel): Agree on default depth=6 but request a mute-level for customer escalation during incidents. Also request explicit Console messaging when compatibility adapter is used.

2025-11-18 Security review (Jonas Meyer): compatibility adapter introduces a surface for data leakage if we buffer streams. Ensure buffers are written to memory only and obey KMS retention and audit logging. Marked security_review_required=true.

2025-11-20 Aisha Kumar: RFC posted, updated PR with deterministic call-hash and provenance TTL=30s. Added integration tests for cyclic flows and streaming partial injection. Marking this ticket In Progress and will start SDK helper PR next week.
